segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Mr. President, I want to thank the leader for his strong words about the importance of making sure that we advance our military leaders when they have been approved for promotion and pay increases. You know, most people are aware that the Senate votes

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: on nominees who have been appointed by the president to occupy top roles in almost all parts of the federal government.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: cabinet secretaries, judges, ambassadors. Less well-known is the fact that the Senate must also vote to approve thousands of military promotions every year. So if a

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: colonel has done well on the job and their services promotion board

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: decides that they're ready to be a brigadier general,
The

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: Senate must vote to approve this promotion before it can go through. Now, typically, this vote is a formality. These promotions are processed in big batches, rather than one at a time, and they usually

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_04
segments.text: happen without even taking a recorded vote. But right now, the Senator from Alabama has

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_05
segments.text: imposed a hold on all

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_05
segments.text: every single senior

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: military nomination and promotion. That means that one senator is personally standing in the way of promotions for 184 of our top-level military

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_06
segments.text: leaders. One senator is holding up pay raises for men and women in uniform. One senator is blocking key senior military leaders from taking their posts.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_06
segments.text: one senator is jeopardizing America's

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: national security. Think for a minute about what this looks like. These holds deprive military families of the pay

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_05
segments.text: increases that they've earned because the nominee's new pay cannot take effect until the promotion goes through.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Without formally being assigned to a change of duty, families can't make decisions

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: right now about moving or enrolling kids in a new school for next school year. The Chief of Staff of the Army has said, "What it really does, it affects the families and some of the kids, and they're trying to figure out where they're going to school, where they're going to move.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: And all those things kind of come into the readiness of the force.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: For families with special needs, there may be even more significant delays to access important

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: services. Secretary Austin has stated that this delay "creates a ripple effect through the force that makes us far less ready than we need

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_06
segments.text: to be."
So,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_06
segments.text: why is one senator punishing 184 dedicated men and women who actively serve in our military? All because he personally disagrees with a single

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: policy decision from the Pentagon.
Now

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: look, it is no secret that I disagree with a lot of policy decisions from the Pentagon. And as senators, we have a lot of tools to shape

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_06
segments.text: and influence government policies. Tools that we can use without putting our national defense at risk. We

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: can pass laws. We can conduct oversight. We can meet with administration officials. We can hold

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: hearings.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: Occasionally, a senator may object to an individual nomination, usually to indicate

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_06
segments.text: opposition to that appointment or to insist on answers

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_04
segments.text: to questions from a federal agency. I've done this myself in the past, as have many of my colleagues on both sides of the aisle.
But that

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_04
segments.text: is not what the senator from Alabama is doing.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_04
segments.text: Instead, he is blocking every single top military

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_05
segments.text: leader from advancing indefinitely. He has snared all 184 top-level service members who are currently slated for

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_06
segments.text: advancement and he has stopped every single one of them dead in their tracks. Like me, the senator from Alabama serves on the Senate Armed Services Committee.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_06
segments.text: And as a consequence, he has many more opportunities than most senators to influence DOD policy. He has many more opportunities to question witnesses, many more opportunities to receive briefings, and many more opportunities to influence the annual defense bill that Congress passes every single year to govern Pentagon operations. He has many opportunities that do not actively threaten our
nation.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_06
segments.text: He has not raised any individual objections to the 184 service members whose promotions are now held up

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: in the Senate, and he has not raised any objections

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_05
segments.text: to the process by which these men and women were vetted and nominated.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_05
segments.text: No, the senator is blocking 184 top

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: military promotions because he disagrees with the Department of Defense policy to help service members and their families access needed health care, specifically to travel to access abortion care. Now, I disagree with the senator on that issue.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: But if he wants to press for votes to reverse DOD's health care policies, he can do that. I will oppose him, but if I lose and if Congress changes the law, then DOD will change its policies. That is how democracy works. Holding up the promotion of every single military nominee isn't democracy, it's

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_06
segments.text: extortion.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_06
segments.text: And that kind of extortion has serious consequences for our national defense.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: These holds pose a grave threat to our national security and to our military readiness. They actively hurt our ability to respond quickly to threats around the world.
Just

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: take a look at the list of 184 people who've already been approved for promotions.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: The 184 people that the senator from Alabama have blocked so far

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_06
segments.text: include nominations for the next commander of the U.S. 5th Fleet in the Middle East, nomination for the next commander of the 7th Fleet in the Pacific.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_06
segments.text: Our next military representative to NATO and the current Director of

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_05
segments.text: Intelligence for U.S. Cyber Command. It includes our next Deputy Chief of Staff for Strategic Deterrence and Nuclear Integration for the Air Force. It includes a top official in Birmingham's Army Reserves. And it includes the former Chief of Staff for Operation Warp Speed.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_05
segments.text: a program the senator from Alabama has repeatedly credited for saving millions of American lives. In fact, the senator from Alabama is single-handedly holding up 11 three-star commanders,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: three recipients of Silver Stars, and three Purple Heart recipients.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: These are brave service

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_06
segments.text: members who deserve better than to be stuck in an administrative hell waiting for a single senator to release them to

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: the promotions and the assignments and the pay increases that

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: their military leaders have determined that they have already earned.
The

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Department of Defense has warned that these blanket holds are making the United States more vulnerable
to

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_05
segments.text: threats from foreign

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_04
segments.text: actors like China, North Korea, and Iran.
In the

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_04
segments.text: coming months, approximately 80

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_04
segments.text: Three- and four-star

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_05
segments.text: generals and admirals, including the leaders of the Army, Navy, and Marine Corps, will reach the end of their current terms, and new nominees will be slotted to replace them. In addition, if the Senator's reckless hold is not lifted, and if the Senate cannot confirm a new chair of the Joint Chiefs of Staff,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_05
segments.text: the President may be without a principal military advisor. By the end of this year, we could have 650

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: general and flag officers waiting for Senate confirmation.
The Senator

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: from Alabama's response to his actions is to say that he will keep these holds in place,
quote,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: until hell freezes over, unless DOD changes its health care travel policy.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_05
segments.text: I sincerely hope that is not true, because holding hostage nearly

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: the entire military leadership of the United States of America at a time when we are facing military threats around the world and our allies are literally engaged in war in Europe is dangerous.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: It is reckless and it needs to stop

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: right now. As chair of the Senate Armed Services Subcommittee on Personnel, I care deeply about protecting our service members and the integrity of our promotion system. These holds are depriving families of pay
raises

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_05
segments.text: that they have earned.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_05
segments.text: We're talking about grocery money for families.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_06
segments.text: These service members are being treated disrespectfully, people who should be treated with dignity and respect. And unless there is some specific problem with an individual nominee, those who have

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: been nominated for a new rank or a new post should get the advancement that the Pentagon

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_05
segments.text: has already recommended for them. No more politics.
I am

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_05
segments.text: here today to respectfully ask my colleague from Alabama to let these promotions move forward

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: and to find other ways to continue advocating for the policy changes that he wants to see. I am hopeful that he will set aside politics and do what is the right thing and allow these service members to carry out their

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_05
segments.text: responsibilities to our nation.
